title: The Alien Space of Science: Sampling Coherent but Cognitively Unavailable Research Directions
abstract: arXiv:2603.01092v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Scientific discovery is constrained not only by what is true, but by what is cognitively available to researchers. Many directions are coherent in light of the literature yet unlikely to be proposed because no existing community combines the relevant concepts, methods, and intuitions. Modern language models inherit this bias, recombining high-density regions of the literature when prompted for novel ideas. We target the complementary region, the alien space of science: directions that are scientifically plausible but unlikely under the distribution of existing researchers. Our method decomposes papers into conceptual units and clusters them into a vocabulary of idea atoms. A coherence model scores whether atom combinations form viable research directions, while an availability model scores whether any existing author community is positioned to produce them. translated_title: 科学的异域空间：采样连贯但认知上不可及的研究方向
translated_abstract: 科学发现不仅受制于什么是真实的，还受制于研究者认知上可及的范围。许多研究方向从文献来看是连贯的，却不太可能被提出，因为没有现有的研究社区同时具备相关的概念、方法和直觉。现代语言模型继承了这种偏见，在被要求提出新想法时往往只会重组文献中的高密度区域。我们瞄准的是与之互补的区域——科学的异域空间：即在科学上合理、但在现有研究者分布下不太可能出现的研究方向。我们的方法将论文分解为概念单元，并将其聚类为一个“想法原子”词表。连贯性模型评估原子的组合能否构成可行的研究方向，而可得性模型评估是否存在任何现有作者群体有能力产出这些方向。我们对组合进行排序，以最大化连贯性并最小化可得性。
tldr: 该论文提出一种方法，通过将文献分解为“想法原子”并联合建模连贯性与认知可得性，来系统性地发现科学上合理但现有研究社区不太可能自发提出的研究方向。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a method that decomposes the literature into "idea atoms" and jointly models coherence and cognitive availability to systematically discover scientifically plausible research directions unlikely to be proposed by existing researcher communities.
